question: In its work programme for 2027, the Commission announced a strategy on the right to stay and a European Care Deal. A study commissioned by the REGI Committee shows that young women leave rural areas more often than young men. In the predominantly rural regions of Germany, there are only 86.8 young women for every 100 young men aged between 15 and 29.

Across the EU, women aged 25-29 in rural areas have an employment rate 11 percentage points lower than that of men, partly due to gaps in childcare and long-term care. Nevertheless, young women in rural areas are not identified as a distinct group in EU funding programmes, and it is not known why they are leaving. This makes it difficult to design policies and assess whether current spending is effective. 1.
Does the Commission intend to collect data on young women in rural areas at NUTS 3 level, as well as data on why they leave these areas or return to them?
Are young women in rural areas identified as a priority group with a measurable target in the ‘right to stay’ strategy?
Does the European Care Deal include specific measures for rural areas where gaps in care provision keep young women out of paid employment?
